// Package encoder provides a fast token-based encoder for the qdf format.
// It serialises Go values into a compact binary representation suitable for
// use as a session-state cache.  The format is designed for low-allocation
// round-trips: a fixed-size header followed by type-tagged fields.
package encoder

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math"
	"reflect"
	"sync"
)

// Version is the current wire-format version.
const Version = 1

// MaxFieldSize is the largest allowed single-field payload in bytes.
const MaxFieldSize = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB

// Tag identifies the type of a field on the wire.
type Tag uint8

const (
	TagInvalid Tag = iota
	TagBool
	TagInt8
	TagInt16
	TagInt32
	TagInt64
	TagUint8
	TagUint16
	TagUint32
	TagUint64
	TagFloat32
	TagFloat64
	TagBytes
	TagString
	TagSlice
	TagMap
	TagStruct
	TagEnd
)

// ErrTruncated is returned when the input buffer ends unexpectedly.
var ErrTruncated = errors.New("encoder: truncated input")

// ErrFieldTooLarge is returned when a single field exceeds MaxFieldSize.
var ErrFieldTooLarge = errors.New("encoder: field too large")

// ErrUnknownTag is returned when an unrecognised tag byte is encountered.
var ErrUnknownTag = errors.New("encoder: unknown tag byte")

// Header is the fixed-size prefix written at the start of every encoded blob.
type Header struct {
	Magic   [4]byte // 'Q','D','F','\x00'
	Version uint8
	Flags   uint8
	_       [2]byte // reserved padding
}

var magicBytes = [4]byte{'Q', 'D', 'F', 0x00}

// encoderPool reuses Encoder values to reduce allocations.
var encoderPool = sync.Pool{New: func() any { return &Encoder{} }}

// Encoder writes qdf-encoded data to an io.Writer.
type Encoder struct {
	w   io.Writer
	buf [8]byte // scratch space for fixed-size integers
	err error
}

// NewEncoder returns an Encoder that writes to w.
func NewEncoder(w io.Writer) *Encoder {
	e := encoderPool.Get().(*Encoder)
	e.w = w
	e.err = nil
	return e
}

// Release returns the Encoder to the pool.  Call after writing is complete.
func (e *Encoder) Release() { encoderPool.Put(e) }

// Err returns the first error encountered during encoding.
func (e *Encoder) Err() error { return e.err }

// WriteHeader writes the fixed 8-byte file header.
func (e *Encoder) WriteHeader() {
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	h := Header{Magic: magicBytes, Version: Version}
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(h.Magic[:])
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	e.buf[0] = h.Version
	e.buf[1] = h.Flags
	e.buf[2] = 0
	e.buf[3] = 0
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(e.buf[:4])
}

// WriteBool writes a boolean field.
func (e *Encoder) WriteBool(v bool) {
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	var b byte
	if v {
		b = 1
	}
	e.buf[0] = byte(TagBool)
	e.buf[1] = b
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(e.buf[:2])
}

// WriteInt64 writes a signed 64-bit integer field.
func (e *Encoder) WriteInt64(v int64) {
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	e.buf[0] = byte(TagInt64)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(e.buf[1:], uint64(v))
	// NOTE: buf is only 8 bytes; we write tag + 7 data bytes then the 8th.
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(e.buf[:8])
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	// The 8th byte of v is stored in a separate write.
	extra := [1]byte{byte(uint64(v) >> 56)}
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(extra[:])
}

// WriteUint64 writes an unsigned 64-bit integer field.
func (e *Encoder) WriteUint64(v uint64) {
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	e.buf[0] = byte(TagUint64)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(e.buf[1:], v)
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(e.buf[:8])
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	extra := [1]byte{byte(v >> 56)}
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(extra[:])
}

// WriteFloat64 writes a 64-bit float field.
func (e *Encoder) WriteFloat64(v float64) {
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	e.buf[0] = byte(TagFloat64)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(e.buf[1:], math.Float64bits(v))
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(e.buf[:8])
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	extra := [1]byte{byte(math.Float64bits(v) >> 56)}
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(extra[:])
}

// WriteBytes writes a byte-slice field with a 4-byte little-endian length prefix.
func (e *Encoder) WriteBytes(v []byte) {
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	if len(v) > MaxFieldSize {
		e.err = ErrFieldTooLarge
		return
	}
	e.buf[0] = byte(TagBytes)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(e.buf[1:], uint32(len(v)))
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(e.buf[:5])
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(v)
}

// WriteString writes a UTF-8 string field.
func (e *Encoder) WriteString(v string) {
	e.WriteBytes([]byte(v))
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	// Overwrite the tag byte with TagString.
	// This is safe because WriteBytes only uses TagBytes.
	// We rely on the fact that the tag was the last byte-slice write.
}

// WriteEnd writes the end-of-record sentinel.
func (e *Encoder) WriteEnd() {
	if e.err != nil {
		return
	}
	e.buf[0] = byte(TagEnd)
	_, e.err = e.w.Write(e.buf[:1])
}

// Decode reads a single field tag from r and dispatches to the appropriate
// typed read function.  It returns the tag and any error.
func Decode(r io.Reader) (Tag, any, error) {
	var tagBuf [1]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, tagBuf[:]); err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, fmt.Errorf("reading tag: %w", err)
	}
	tag := Tag(tagBuf[0])
	switch tag {
	case TagBool:
		return decodeBool(r)
	case TagInt64:
		return decodeInt64(r)
	case TagUint64:
		return decodeUint64(r)
	case TagFloat64:
		return decodeFloat64(r)
	case TagBytes:
		return decodeBytes(r)
	case TagString:
		return decodeString(r)
	case TagEnd:
		return TagEnd, nil, nil
	default:
		return TagInvalid, nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: 0x%02x", ErrUnknownTag, uint8(tag))
	}
}

func decodeBool(r io.Reader) (Tag, any, error) {
	var buf [1]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf[:]); err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, ErrTruncated
	}
	return TagBool, buf[0] != 0, nil
}

func decodeInt64(r io.Reader) (Tag, any, error) {
	var buf [8]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf[:]); err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, ErrTruncated
	}
	v := int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[:]))
	return TagInt64, v, nil
}

func decodeUint64(r io.Reader) (Tag, any, error) {
	var buf [8]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf[:]); err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, ErrTruncated
	}
	v := binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[:])
	return TagUint64, v, nil
}

func decodeFloat64(r io.Reader) (Tag, any, error) {
	var buf [8]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf[:]); err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, ErrTruncated
	}
	v := math.Float64frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[:]))
	return TagFloat64, v, nil
}

func decodeBytes(r io.Reader) (Tag, any, error) {
	var lenBuf [4]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, lenBuf[:]); err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, ErrTruncated
	}
	n := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(lenBuf[:])
	if n > MaxFieldSize {
		return TagInvalid, nil, ErrFieldTooLarge
	}
	data := make([]byte, n)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, data); err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, ErrTruncated
	}
	return TagBytes, data, nil
}

func decodeString(r io.Reader) (Tag, any, error) {
	_, v, err := decodeBytes(r)
	if err != nil {
		return TagInvalid, nil, err
	}
	return TagString, string(v.([]byte)), nil
}

// reflectEncode uses reflection to encode arbitrary struct values.
// It is slower than hand-written encoders but useful for testing.
func reflectEncode(e *Encoder, v reflect.Value) error {
	switch v.Kind() {
	case reflect.Bool:
		e.WriteBool(v.Bool())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		e.WriteInt64(v.Int())
	case reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64:
		e.WriteUint64(v.Uint())
	case reflect.Float32, reflect.Float64:
		e.WriteFloat64(v.Float())
	case reflect.String:
		e.WriteString(v.String())
	case reflect.Slice:
		if v.Type().Elem().Kind() == reflect.Uint8 {
			e.WriteBytes(v.Bytes())
		} else {
			return fmt.Errorf("encoder: unsupported slice element type %s", v.Type().Elem())
		}
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("encoder: unsupported kind %s", v.Kind())
	}
	return e.Err()
}
